key.description: Shown once: store it now, it cannot be shown again.
key.title: Key

CandidateDetailOut.description:
A candidate as the reviewer reads it: for an UPDATE or DELETE of an entry, that entry as
it is now (what the decision would obsolete).
CandidateDetailOut.title: CandidateDetailOut

review_policy.description: How low and medium risk are routed, e.g. {"low": "review"}: "auto" (live at once), "user" (ask the end user), "review" (a reviewer). High risk always goes to review.
review_policy.title: Review Policy

review_policy.description: How low and medium risk are routed, e.g. {"low": "review"}: "auto" (live at once), "user" (ask the end user), "review" (a reviewer). High risk always goes to review.
review_policy.title: Review Policy

user_id.description: The end user answering their card. Without it, the key's own role decides (the review queue needs a key with the review scope).
user_id.title: User Id

DocumentOut.description:
`state` is the governed lifecycle (as for entries); `status` is the KB provider's parse
status. Only an active/verified document with status `ready` is retrieved.
DocumentOut.title: DocumentOut

DocumentWritten.description: An upload: the document, and the candidate when it waits for a reviewer.
DocumentWritten.title: DocumentWritten

risk_level.description: Your own estimate; the rules (keywords, personal data) can only raise it.

user_id.description: The end user to ask about medium-risk knowledge (a confirmation card).
user_id.title: User Id

EntryVersionOut.description: One version of an entry: what its text was from `changed_at` on.
EntryVersionOut.title: EntryVersionOut

mode.description: async: buffer and extract later. sync: extract now and return the memories.
mode.title: Mode

ErasedOut.description: What one user's erasure removed (counts only).
ErasedOut.title: ErasedOut

item_id.description: One of the items this retrieval returned.
item_id.title: Item Id

MemoryBrief.description: One version of a fact in a supersede chain.
MemoryBrief.title: MemoryBrief

infer.description: Let the memory provider extract facts. Needs the 'extract' capability (P2).
infer.title: Infer

key.description: Profile key (e.g. user.city): one current value per user (and agent); a new value supersedes the old one. Not allowed together with session_id.
key.title: Key

user_id.description: Who to ask (default: the memory's owner).
user_id.title: User Id

metadata.description: Exact values; KB documents carry none.
metadata.title: Metadata

as_of.description: What was valid at this moment (superseded memories included).
as_of.title: As Of

include_pinned.description: Put the user's pinned memories and profile values first.
include_pinned.title: Include Pinned

rerank.description: Re-score the best fused candidates with a cross-encoder. Default: the namespace's `retrieval.rerank` (off).
rerank.title: Rerank

token_budget.description: Default: the namespace's (2000). Estimated tokens of the returned items.
token_budget.title: Token Budget

degraded.description: What failed or ran out of time; the rest of the response stands.
degraded.title: Degraded

suggestions.description: The scope's user's open confirmation cards (design §5).
suggestions.title: Suggestions

kind.description: A KB hit is an entry, or a document (its matching chunks, not the file).
kind.title: Kind

passages.description: A document's matching chunks, best first; `content` is them joined.
passages.title: Passages

ttl_seconds.description: Lifetime in seconds: 15 minutes by default, 1 hour at most.
ttl_seconds.title: Ttl Seconds

Written.description: A write is either live knowledge (`entry`) or a candidate waiting for someone.
Written.title: Written

AdminToken.description: The Admin's static token (STEWARD_ADMIN_TOKEN); no login, no accounts

UserToken.description: A user token from POST /v1/tokens/user: only that end user's own data

post.description: A reviewer's rejection says why (design §9): `note` is required here.

patch.description: A new version (the admin reviews, so it applies at once; the text is screened).

get.description: Every version, newest first: an edit's `before` is the text the previous version had.

post.description: The key is in this answer once and never again (only its hash is kept).

Rewritten as general knowledge (needs the KB LLM) into `collection_id`, else the
namespace's suggestion collection; proposed for review, like any agent's suggestion.

The missing answer to a retrieval, proposed as knowledge: a candidate for review (the
admin writes it, a reviewer approves it; the log is its source).
The Playground: the same retrieval as `/v1/retrieve`, logged like it.

put.description: The whole config, as YAML, validated before anything is written (`steward ns apply`).

get.description: Most recently active first. `cursor` is the previous page's `next_cursor` (opaque).
Unauthenticated (see deps.UNAUTHENTICATED_PATHS): component status only, no data.

post.description: Store conversation messages for memory extraction (design §5).
Extract this scope's buffered episodes now instead of waiting for size or idle time.

get.description:
An outbox job's status (design §7): pending, running, done or failed, with its attempts and
its last error (already redacted). Its payload is internal and not shown.

post.description:
A `file`, or a `url` to import (exactly one). Stored, then handed to the KB provider by the
worker (202); a URL is fetched by the worker first (public https only; the namespace's
`documents.url_allowlist` limits hosts), and a fetch that cannot succeed fails the document.
Routed by the collection: high risk waits for a reviewer (`candidate`), a reviewer's upload
is verified, others go live. The title is screened like an entry's; the content is parsed by
the provider, not screened.

delete.description:
Out of retrieval at once, out of the provider when the Syncer runs (the row is kept); a
document waiting for review is rejected instead.

post.description:
Submitted, then routed by risk (design §5): low goes live, medium asks `user_id` (or goes
live without one), high waits for a reviewer. Personal data is redacted (namespace policy).

patch.description: A new version. Verified knowledge, or a high-risk edit, waits for a reviewer (202).

post.description: Out of retrieval at once (the safety net), out of the provider when the Syncer runs.

delete.description:
Erase everything llm-steward holds about one end user (GDPR-style; the one exception to
"invalidate, never delete"): their memories and those memories' history, their episodes,
their open cards and their retrieval logs. Engine copies are removed by the outbox. Team
knowledge they helped decide stays. API keys only.
Soft delete: the memory becomes `deleted` and is removed from the provider by the Syncer.

patch.description: Pin, re-weight or re-tag. New content is a new memory (POST) that supersedes this one.

get.description: Every change to this memory, and every version of the fact (the supersede chain).

post.description:
Rewrite the memory as general knowledge (`kb.draft`), then route it like any KB write:
201 live, 202 a candidate. Needs the KB LLM (STEWARD_KB_LLM).

get.description:
A user's current profile values (key -> value) and the pinned memories they see: the same
core memories `/v1/retrieve` always puts in the context. A user token reads its own.

post.description: Joint search over memory and KB: 200 with `degraded` if a source failed, 503 if all did.
Was a returned item helpful? Recorded per answer; KB entries count it.

The host app proposes saving `text` to the KB (design §7): drafted by `kb.draft`, then
routed by risk (201 live, 202 a candidate, a card when `user_id` is asked). Needs the KB LLM.
API keys only: under a user token the card would ask the same user, who could then approve
their own text into the shared KB.

A short-lived token for one end user, for calling llm-steward from their browser (design
§7). It reaches only that user's own memories, cards and retrievals; revoking the API key that
minted it ends it. Your server calls this with its API key; never ship the key to a browser.
503 when the server has no STEWARD_TOKEN_SECRET.
